title: MTH 602 HW1 bonus competition presentation
goal: Create a concise 5–10 minute MTH 602 class presentation and natural talking points that faithfully explain the actual Homework 1 bonus coefficient-recovery methodology, show how the analysis narrowed to two exact candidate coefficient vectors, explain why the sparse rational candidate was chosen from the evidence available before submission, and reveal only at the end that the competing Taylor candidate was the hidden true answer even though the sparse submission still won the class competition.
acceptance_criteria: The presentation fits naturally in 5–10 minutes and is approximately 5–7 slides, with no unnecessary technical detours.
The deck accurately distinguishes the competition objective of coefficient-vector recovery from ordinary prediction fit and uses the ill-conditioned degree-9 OLS result to motivate the deeper search.
The presentation shows how sparse model selection and structural pattern recognition narrowed the problem to the sparse rational candidate and the degree-9 Taylor candidate of sin(2t).
Only evidence actually available before submission is used to justify the submitted sparse rational candidate; post-submission information is not retroactively used as methodology.

The explanation of why the sparse candidate was chosen is faithful to the durable analysis: sparse/BIC support, coefficient values near simple rationals, weak bootstrap support for Taylor tail terms, slightly better residual statistics, and generic Gaussian comparisons, while acknowledging the unstated +/-0.01 hard-bound clue favoring Taylor.
The fact that the Taylor candidate was actually correct is withheld until the final reveal/outcome slide.
The final reveal explains that the sparse submission still won the class competition because it was the closest submitted coefficient vector, not because it matched the hidden vector exactly.
AI assistance in presentation preparation does not alter or invent the historical methodology; project-owned source notes and numerical records remain authoritative.
Talking points are concise prompts/transitions rather than a word-for-word script.
Visuals are legible and directly support the story, especially the unstable OLS fit, two-candidate comparison, model-support evidence, and final reveal.
The PowerPoint is structurally checked, rendered, visually reviewed, and revised as needed before delivery.
constraints: Use the isolated MTH602 branch hw1-bonus-presentation created from b297c524d505715fe93f9a266d7d45564cbbe47f.
Mutate only homework/hw01/presentation/** unless a later explicit task decision broadens scope.
Do not rewrite homework/hw01/records/bonus_analysis.json or the historical bonus submission to make the methodology look cleaner in hindsight.
Treat homework/hw01/presentation/SOURCE_NOTES.md and homework/hw01/records/bonus_analysis.json as the primary pre-submission methodology/evidence sources.
Treat the student's statement that the Taylor candidate was the hidden true answer as post-competition outcome evidence and reveal it only at the end.
Keep the deck suitable for ordinary class participation rather than a research talk; prioritize the decision story over exhaustive derivations.
Do not present AI as part of the mathematical methodology unless needed to answer a direct class question about allowed tooling.
External delivery/presentation remains a user action.
